name: Cockatiel
nativeRange: Australian mainland, favouring arid and semi-arid regions
colors: Grey body, white wing patches, yellow face and crest, orange cheek patches
habitat: Open woodland, scrubland, and grassland near water sources
feedingGuide: Provide a quality seed mix supplemented with fresh vegetables, fruits, and occasional protein. Ensure constant access to fresh water and cuttlebone for calcium.
behavior: Known for whistling and mimicking sounds. Males tend to be more vocal. Form strong bonds with owners.
whereToFind: Widely available at pet stores and breeders worldwide
description: The cockatiel, also known as the weero or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member. Native to Australia, it is the sole member of the genus Nymphicus.

name: Budgerigar
nativeRange: Open habitats across Australia, avoiding coastal areas and dense forests
colors: Naturally green and yellow with black scalloped markings; captive-bred in blues, whites, yellows, greys, and crested varieties
habitat: Open grasslands, scrublands, and woodland edges
diet: Grass seeds, occasionally insects and vegetation
feedingGuide: Offer a balanced seed or pellet diet with daily fresh greens. Millet sprays make excellent treats. Avoid avocado and chocolate.
behavior: Highly social flock birds. Can learn to mimic words and whistles. Best kept in pairs or small groups.
whereToFind: One of the most widely available pet birds globally
description: The budgerigar, also known as the common parakeet, shell parakeet or budgie, is a small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot native to Australia. Naturally, the species is green and yellow with black, scalloped markings on the nape, back, and wings.

name: African Grey Parrot
nativeRange: Equatorial Africa, from Côte d'Ivoire to Kenya
colors: Predominantly grey plumage with a bright red tail
habitat: Lowland rainforest, forest edges, and gallery forests
feedingGuide: High-quality pellets supplemented with fresh fruits, vegetables, and nuts. Requires mental stimulation during feeding with foraging toys.
behavior: Renowned for exceptional talking and cognitive abilities. Requires significant social interaction and mental enrichment.
whereToFind: Specialty breeders and avian rescue organizations
description: The grey parrot, also known as the Congo grey parrot, is an African parrot in the family Psittacidae. Psittacus erithacus was previously also known as the African grey parrot until the Timneh parrot was elevated to a full species.

name: Lovebird
colors: Varies by species — green, peach-faced, yellow, blue, and mixed mutations in captivity
habitat: Open woodland, savanna, and semi-arid regions
feedingGuide: Seed mix or pellets with daily fresh produce. Pairs should be fed together to prevent food guarding.
behavior: Named for their strong monogamous pair bonding. Social birds that spend long periods sitting together. Best kept in pairs.
whereToFind: Pet stores and breeders specializing in small parrots
description: Lovebird is the common name for the genus Agapornis, a small group of parrots in the Old World parrot family Psittaculidae. Social and affectionate, the name comes from the parrots' strong, monogamous pair bonding.

name: Sun Conure
colors: Golden-yellow plumage with orange-flushed face and underparts, green and blue-tipped wings and tail
habitat: Tropical forests, forest edges, and palm groves
diet: Fruits, flowers, berries, seeds, nuts, and insects
feedingGuide: Varied diet of pellets, fresh fruits, vegetables, and occasional nuts. High-energy birds need nutrient-dense food.
behavior: Very social, typically living in flocks. Form monogamous pairs. Known for loud vocalizations.
description: The sun conure, also known as the sun parakeet, is a medium-sized, vibrantly colored parrot native to northeastern South America. Sun conures are now listed as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

name: Eclectus Parrot
nativeRange: New Guinea, northeastern Australia, and surrounding islands
colors: Males bright green; females predominantly bright red and purple-blue
feedingGuide: Fresh fruits and vegetables are essential. Low-fat diet compared to other parrots. Avoid excessive seeds.
behavior: Males and females were once thought to be different species due to extreme sexual dimorphism. Do well in captivity.
description: Eclectus is a genus of parrot consisting of four known extant species. Males are mostly bright green, females are predominantly bright red. The male and female eclectus were once thought to be different species.

name: Zebra Finch
nativeRange: Central and eastern Australia, also found in Indonesia
colors: Grey head, white and black barred tail, orange cheek patches, chestnut flanks with white spots on males
lifespan: 2–3 years in the wild; 5–7 years in captivity
habitat: Open steppes, grasslands, and open areas with scattered bushes
feedingGuide: Canary seed mix with millet, fresh greens, and egg food during breeding season.
behavior: Travel in large flocks in the wild. Males sing complex songs to attract mates.
description: The zebra finches are two species of estrildid finch in the genus Taeniopygia found in Australia and Indonesia. They are seed-eaters that travel in large flocks.

name: Society Finch
origin: Domesticated in China; imported to Europe via Japan in the 1860s
nativeRange: Not found in the wild; domesticated form
colors: Brown, white, and fawn variations; some pied and crested mutations
feedingGuide: Standard finch seed mix with fresh vegetables. Excellent for community aviaries.
behavior: Known for communal nesting — multiple pairs may share a nest. Popular foster parents for other finch species.
description: The Society finch, also known as the Bengali finch or Bengalese finch, is a domesticated subspecies of estrildid finch. It became a popular cage and trade bird after appearing in European zoos in the 1860s.

name: Gouldian Finch
nativeRange: Northern Australia, particularly the Kimberley region
colors: Red, black, or yellow head; green back; purple chest; yellow belly
diet: Grass seeds, particularly during dry season
feedingGuide: Requires specialized finch mix with live food during breeding. Sensitive to air quality — avoid drafts.
description: The Gouldian finch, also known as the Gould's finch or the rainbow finch, is a colourful passerine bird that is native to Australia.

name: Diamond Dove
nativeRange: Central, western, and northern Australia; occasionally southern Australia
colors: Grey-brown body with white spots on wings, orange eye ring, small size
habitat: Lightly arid or semi-arid areas near water
feedingGuide: Dove or finch seed mix with grit and fresh water. Small portions of greens occasionally.
behavior: One of Australia's smallest pigeons. Ground-feeding birds that prefer calm environments.
description: The diamond dove is a resident bird in Australia. They are one of Australia's smallest pigeons along with the peaceful dove.

name: Ring-necked Dove
nativeRange: Sub-Saharan Africa, from Ethiopia to South Africa
colors: Pale brown-grey body with semi-collar of black feathers on lower nape
habitat: Open habitats including savanna, woodland edges, and agricultural areas
feedingGuide: Dove seed mix with access to grit. Fresh greens and soft foods during breeding.
behavior: Mostly sedentary. Known for rhythmic three-syllabled cooing. Congregates at waterholes in dry regions.
description: The ring-necked dove, also known as the Cape turtle dove, is a widespread and often abundant dove species in East and southern Africa. Its name is derived from the semi-collar of black feathers on the lower nape.

name: Canary
origin: Macaronesian Islands (domesticated form of wild canary)
nativeRange: Canary Islands, Madeira, and Azores (wild ancestor)
colors: Wide variety — yellow, orange, red, white, and variegated through selective breeding
diet: Canary seed mix, fresh greens, and egg food
feedingGuide: Quality canary seed blend with daily fresh greens. Cuttlebone for calcium. Separate feeding dishes for multiple birds.
behavior: Males are prized for their singing ability. Over 500 years of selective breeding for color and song.
description: The domestic canary, often simply known as the canary, is a domesticated form and subspecies of the wild canary, a small songbird in the finch family originating in the Macaronesian Islands.
